title: sse: fix partial JSON delimiter and token/event ordering in SSE streaming
author: Ava Kim
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming bug where partial-JSON events and token/event frames could be emitted in the wrong order, causing consumers (OpenAI-compat clients and structured-output parsers) to receive malformed partial JSON. No breaking changes to the public API; rolling upgrade safe.
description:
Context: Several customers and our internal canaries observed intermittent JSON parse errors when consuming server-sent events (SSE) from streaming endpoints (chat/generate/stream). Root cause: under high-concurrency and when partial-JSON structured events are emitted alongside raw token/event frames, the encoder could emit delimiters ("\n\n" chunk boundaries and structured-event separators) in an ordering that allowed a consumer to see a token event before the structured-event delimiter, producing an invalid partial JSON object. This manifested as: - Broken partial JSON objects in OpenAI-compat streaming responses - Structured output parsers failing to reassemble partial JSON across frames - Sporadic downstream tool-calling failures (tool payloads truncated).

This PR fixes the emitter ordering and makes the framing deterministic. Changes made: 1) sse: rework encoder state machine so structured-event delimiters are emitted before token frames when both are pending (pkg/sse/encoder.go). This ensures a consumer always sees an opening delimiter for a partial JSON object before any token/event frames that belong to it. 2) parser: strengthen the streaming parser to tolerate boundary cases and to validate delimiter tokens more strictly to avoid accidental merge across adjacent events (pkg/sse/parser.go). 3) openai-compat: align streaming translation to downstream OpenAI-compat framing rules so third-party clients relying on ordering semantics continue to work (internal/openai_compat/streaming.go). 4) SDKs: add a small defensive decode path in python SDK streaming helper to buffer until a complete delimiter sequence is received (sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py). 5) Tests: unit tests for encoder/parser plus an integration canary that runs a high-concurrency producer against the consumer harness to reproduce previous failures and assert no invalid partial JSON observed (pkg/sse/encoder_test.go, integration/streaming_test.go). 6) Docs: update SSE streaming docs with the clarified framing contract and migration notes (docs/sse.md).

Testing: - Local unit test coverage updated for encoder/parser (new test vectors for interleaved token+structured events). - Added integration canary (reproduces scenario from ENG-1245) which passed on CI. - E2E run against the OpenAI-compat client harness showed no partial-json parse errors across 10k generated events.

Rollout: merged to main and deployed to staging; will be included in next patch release. Backwards compatibility: encoder changes preserve existing delimiter characters and framing tokens; consumers that currently tolerate the previous non-determinism continue to work, but now receive deterministic ordering which is safer for structured-output and tool-calling consumers.

notes: This is a high-priority runtime fix affecting streaming stability and structured output reliability. Recommend monitoring 'sse.parser.errors' and 'openai_compat.partial_json_failures' for the next 48 hours after rollout. If any downstream SDKs observe errors, roll forward the defensive buffering in SDKs as a temporary mitigation.
